name: Wizehawk Store Discovery Audit
author: Wizehawk

sections.description:
Wizehawk Store Discovery Audit helps WooCommerce merchants see whether their public store is understandable and accessible to AI search and shopping systems.

Current checks include:

  • robots.txt reachability and OpenAI crawler directives
  • WordPress search visibility and sitemap availability
  • WooCommerce product data quality
  • WooCommerce-generated Product JSON-LD, including offers, price, currency, availability, image, SKU, GTIN, and brand when applicable
  • optional per-product Live Page Deep Test on public stores
  • final rendered page indexability and canonical URL
  • final rendered Product JSON-LD and duplicate Product schema detection
  • local scan history stored in the WordPress database
  • live-page results stored locally as product metadata

No Wizehawk account or Wizehawk cloud service is required for manual scanning. The plugin does use the external services disclosed below for crawler verification and optional licensing/usage services.

Privacy and activity monitoring

AI activity monitoring is disabled by default. An administrator must explicitly enable it in Store Discovery Audit > Settings before real crawler/referral activity is recorded.

When monitoring is enabled, the plugin stores recognized event type/source, requested path, related WooCommerce product ID (when applicable), verification result, and event time in the site’s own WordPress database. Visitor IP addresses are never stored. User-agent strings and referrer URLs are used only during the current request to recognize a supported crawler/referral and are not stored.

For supported crawlers, the visitor IP is compared locally against official published crawler IP ranges. The visitor IP is not sent to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Perplexity by this plugin.

External services

This plugin uses the following external services. These requests are limited to the purposes described here.

OpenAI

For recognized OpenAI crawler requests, the plugin may download OpenAI’s publicly published crawler IP-range JSON files so it can verify the crawler locally.

Data sent: a normal HTTPS request from the WordPress server to OpenAI’s published JSON endpoint. The request identifies this plugin in its user-agent. No WooCommerce product data, visitor IP address, referrer URL, or visitor user-agent is sent by the plugin.

When: only when verification is needed for a recognized supported OpenAI crawler and a cached list is not available.

Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/
Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/

Anthropic / Claude

For recognized Anthropic/Claude crawler requests, the plugin may download Anthropic’s publicly published crawler IP-range JSON file so it can verify the crawler locally.

Data sent: a normal HTTPS request from the WordPress server to Anthropic’s published JSON endpoint. The request identifies this plugin in its user-agent. No WooCommerce product data, visitor IP address, referrer URL, or visitor user-agent is sent by the plugin.

When: only when verification is needed for a recognized supported Anthropic crawler and a cached list is not available.

Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms
Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

Perplexity

For recognized Perplexity crawler requests, the plugin may download Perplexity’s publicly published crawler IP-range JSON files so it can verify the crawler locally.

Data sent: a normal HTTPS request from the WordPress server to Perplexity’s published JSON endpoint. The request identifies this plugin in its user-agent. No WooCommerce product data, visitor IP address, referrer URL, or visitor user-agent is sent by the plugin.

When: only when verification is needed for a recognized supported Perplexity crawler and a cached list is not available.

Terms: https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/terms-of-service
Privacy: https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/privacy-policy

Freemius

This plugin uses the Freemius SDK for optional usage analytics, upgrade/checkout links, licensing, and paid add-on management.

On activation, Freemius presents an opt-in choice before optional usage data is shared. If the administrator opts in, Freemius may receive site/admin and environment information such as the administrator name/email, site URL, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions, and diagnostic environment information. If the administrator skips the opt-in, optional usage analytics are not sent.

When a paid add-on is purchased or a license is activated/managed, the information needed for checkout, licensing, account management, and updates is sent to Freemius as part of that requested operation.

Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/
Privacy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Free and Pro

The Free version provides the complete manual AI-commerce audit: manual store scans, crawler/discovery checks, product readiness, AI-readable Product JSON-LD checks, live-page testing, basic 7-day AI activity counts, and the three most recent scan summaries.

Pro adds automatic daily scans, regression monitoring, hosted email alerts, longer scan history and automatic comparisons, bulk product fixes, and advanced AI activity reporting.

How to upgrade to Pro

Store Discovery Audit Pro is a separate add-on plugin. Keep the Free plugin installed and active.

  1. Open Store Discovery Audit and click Upgrade to Pro.
  2. Choose the yearly plan and finish checkout.
  3. Download the Store Discovery Audit Pro ZIP. Do not unzip it.
  4. Go to Plugins > Add Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  5. Choose the Pro ZIP, click Install Now, then Activate Plugin.
  6. Leave both Store Discovery Audit and Store Discovery Audit Pro active.
  7. If asked for a license, use the Activate License button shown by Store Discovery Audit.
  8. Open Store Discovery Audit again. The badge beside the version should say Pro.

Do not delete or replace the Free plugin. Free is the core plugin; Pro adds the paid features.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP in Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Store Discovery Audit in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Click Run store scan.

0.3.5

  • Adds a visible live-test cooldown timer before another request can be sent.
  • Disables all live-test buttons during cooldown so repeated clicks cannot trigger avoidable 429 responses.
  • Shows a clear “Too many attempts / cooling down” message with the remaining wait time.
  • Treats blocked/rate-limited live tests as completed diagnostics rather than generic AJAX errors.

0.3.4

  • Caches discovery checks for 15 minutes to reduce repeat requests.
  • Treats HTTP 403/429/503 discovery responses as temporary access limits rather than permanent failures.
  • Preserves the last successful discovery state when a temporary rate limit occurs.
  • Adds live-page request cooldowns and longer backoff after a security/rate-limit response.

0.3.3

  • Compare multiple rendered Product JSON-LD objects instead of warning on duplicate count alone.
  • Treat consistent overlapping product schema values as harmless duplication.
  • Warn only when duplicate Product schemas disagree on product name, SKU, GTIN, brand, price, currency, or availability.

0.3.2

  • Treat HTTP 403, 429, and 503 as an unavailable live test instead of a product failure.
  • Skip downstream canonical and schema checks when the public page could not be retrieved.
  • Identify live-page requests with a descriptive Wizehawk user agent.

0.3.1

  • Live-page results now include an expandable list of every blocking issue and warning instead of showing only the first finding.
  • Added a public-product-content check to flag cases where an outside request appears to receive a coming-soon page, maintenance screen, login wall, security challenge, redirect, or other interstitial instead of the product itself.
  • Keeps live-page findings separate from the fast store scan and stores the detailed result locally.

0.3.0

  • Added optional per-product Live Page Deep Test for public stores.
  • Verifies final rendered HTML, indexability, canonical URL, Product JSON-LD, duplicate Product schemas, offers, price, currency, availability, image, SKU, GTIN, and brand.
  • Live tests are separate from the fast store scan to avoid slowing large catalogs.
  • Local/development sites show the live test as unavailable until a public URL is used.

0.2.2

  • Separates WooCommerce product-data findings from machine-readable schema findings in the product table.
  • Adds independent severity counts for each layer to avoid double-counting confusion.
  • Clarifies that the overall product status reflects both layers.

0.2.1

  • Tightened machine-readable Product schema checks so missing offer price, currency, availability, image, and SKU are no longer incorrectly reported as Ready.

0.2.0

  • Added WooCommerce Product JSON-LD readiness checks.
  • Checks offer price, currency, availability, image, SKU, GTIN, and brand exposure.
  • Added Machine data status to each product row.
  • Added schema-specific fix labels and dashboard guidance.

0.1.3

  • Renamed the dashboard summary from “Blocking issues” to “Products blocked” so the label accurately describes the count.

0.1.2

  • Local/development sites no longer show a misleading sitemap timeout warning when WordPress cannot request its own local URL.
  • Product fix lists can now be expanded to show every blocking issue and warning.
  • Each fix is labeled as Blocking or Warning for clearer prioritization.

0.1.1

  • Fixed admin menu visibility when WooCommerce is not installed or active.
  • Plugin administration now uses the standard WordPress administrator capability and still requires WooCommerce only for product scanning.

0.1.0

  • Initial private development build.

short_description: Local-first WooCommerce readiness checks for AI search discovery, crawler access, and structured product information.
description:
Wizehawk Store Discovery Audit helps WooCommerce merchants see whether their public store is understandable and accessible to AI search and shopping systems.

Current checks include:

  • robots.txt reachability and OpenAI crawler directives
  • WordPress search visibility and sitemap availability
  • WooCommerce product data quality
  • WooCommerce-generated Product JSON-LD, including offers, price, currency, availability, image, SKU, GTIN, and brand when applicable
  • optional per-product Live Page Deep Test on public stores
  • final rendered page indexability and canonical URL
  • final rendered Product JSON-LD and duplicate Product schema detection
  • local scan history stored in the WordPress database
  • live-page results stored locally as product metadata

No Wizehawk account or Wizehawk cloud service is required for manual scanning. The plugin does use the external services disclosed below for crawler verification and optional licensing/usage services.

Privacy and activity monitoring

AI activity monitoring is disabled by default. An administrator must explicitly enable it in Store Discovery Audit > Settings before real crawler/referral activity is recorded.

When monitoring is enabled, the plugin stores recognized event type/source, requested path, related WooCommerce product ID (when applicable), verification result, and event time in the site’s own WordPress database. Visitor IP addresses are never stored. User-agent strings and referrer URLs are used only during the current request to recognize a supported crawler/referral and are not stored.

For supported crawlers, the visitor IP is compared locally against official published crawler IP ranges. The visitor IP is not sent to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Perplexity by this plugin.

External services

This plugin uses the following external services. These requests are limited to the purposes described here.

OpenAI

For recognized OpenAI crawler requests, the plugin may download OpenAI’s publicly published crawler IP-range JSON files so it can verify the crawler locally.

Data sent: a normal HTTPS request from the WordPress server to OpenAI’s published JSON endpoint. The request identifies this plugin in its user-agent. No WooCommerce product data, visitor IP address, referrer URL, or visitor user-agent is sent by the plugin.

When: only when verification is needed for a recognized supported OpenAI crawler and a cached list is not available.

Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/
Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/

Anthropic / Claude

For recognized Anthropic/Claude crawler requests, the plugin may download Anthropic’s publicly published crawler IP-range JSON file so it can verify the crawler locally.

Data sent: a normal HTTPS request from the WordPress server to Anthropic’s published JSON endpoint. The request identifies this plugin in its user-agent. No WooCommerce product data, visitor IP address, referrer URL, or visitor user-agent is sent by the plugin.

When: only when verification is needed for a recognized supported Anthropic crawler and a cached list is not available.

Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms
Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

Perplexity

For recognized Perplexity crawler requests, the plugin may download Perplexity’s publicly published crawler IP-range JSON files so it can verify the crawler locally.

Data sent: a normal HTTPS request from the WordPress server to Perplexity’s published JSON endpoint. The request identifies this plugin in its user-agent. No WooCommerce product data, visitor IP address, referrer URL, or visitor user-agent is sent by the plugin.

When: only when verification is needed for a recognized supported Perplexity crawler and a cached list is not available.

Terms: https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/terms-of-service
Privacy: https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/privacy-policy

Freemius

This plugin uses the Freemius SDK for optional usage analytics, upgrade/checkout links, licensing, and paid add-on management.

On activation, Freemius presents an opt-in choice before optional usage data is shared. If the administrator opts in, Freemius may receive site/admin and environment information such as the administrator name/email, site URL, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions, and diagnostic environment information. If the administrator skips the opt-in, optional usage analytics are not sent.

When a paid add-on is purchased or a license is activated/managed, the information needed for checkout, licensing, account management, and updates is sent to Freemius as part of that requested operation.

Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/
Privacy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Free and Pro

The Free version provides the complete manual AI-commerce audit: manual store scans, crawler/discovery checks, product readiness, AI-readable Product JSON-LD checks, live-page testing, basic 7-day AI activity counts, and the three most recent scan summaries.

Pro adds automatic daily scans, regression monitoring, hosted email alerts, longer scan history and automatic comparisons, bulk product fixes, and advanced AI activity reporting.

How to upgrade to Pro

Store Discovery Audit Pro is a separate add-on plugin. Keep the Free plugin installed and active.

  1. Open Store Discovery Audit and click Upgrade to Pro.
  2. Choose the yearly plan and finish checkout.
  3. Download the Store Discovery Audit Pro ZIP. Do not unzip it.
  4. Go to Plugins > Add Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  5. Choose the Pro ZIP, click Install Now, then Activate Plugin.
  6. Leave both Store Discovery Audit and Store Discovery Audit Pro active.
  7. If asked for a license, use the Activate License button shown by Store Discovery Audit.
  8. Open Store Discovery Audit again. The badge beside the version should say Pro.

Do not delete or replace the Free plugin. Free is the core plugin; Pro adds the paid features.
